title: ISic004523. Dedication by the Akragantines to Apollo at Delphi
body:
Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa
1[Ἀ]κραγαντῖνοι τ[ο͂ι Ἀπό-]
2λο̄νι (vac.)

Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa
1[.]ΚΡΑΓΑΝΤΙΝΟΙΤ[......]
2ΛΟ̄ΝΙ      

Apparatus criticus

  • Text after Arena 2002 (IGASMG II² 94). ;
  • lines.1–2: Arena prints the dialectal form Ἀπόλο̄νι and regularises it as Ἀπόλλωνι. ;
  • Because the original width of the base cannot be established, the restoration remains uncertain. Dubois 1989 records the alternatives τ[ῶι Ἀπόλ]λωνι and τ[ὸ ἄγαλμα τῶι Ἀπόλ]λωνι; Arena 2002 adopts the former.

English translation

Valentina Mignosa

The Akragantines [dedicated this] to Apollo.

commentary

Bousquet tentatively dated the dedication to the second quarter of the 5th century BCE and suggested a connection with the establishment of democracy at Akragas after the fall of the tyranny and the death of Theron in 472 BCE. De Waele, drawing on Aelian, Varia Historia 2.33, conjectured that the base may have supported the ivory statue of the river-god Akragas said to have been dedicated at Delphi by the Akragantines in commemoration of the advent of democracy in 471 BCE. Both historical identifications remain conjectural. Bousquet distinguished this smaller base from the other Akragantine dedication at Delphi, inv. 5098 (Dubois 182b).

bibliography

  • Bousquet 1959 149–150, fig. 4 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10001375
  • De Waele 1971 39–40 no. 8, pl. 10 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10002040
  • Lazzarini 1976 905 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10002517
  • Dubois 1989 182a https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10000187
  • Jeffery and Johnston 1990 Addenda, 372 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10000678
  • Arena 2002 94 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10001373

Bousquet notes rho with a triangular loop and a tail, alpha with an oblique crossbar descending to the foot of the right hasta, lunate sigma, and nu with an oblique left hasta and an almost vertical right hasta.

Lines 1–2 18–21
